text:
zoe: Quick thread: we need to decide on 'data provenance' guarantees for audit exports. Two asks from customers: (A) tamper-proof timestamping for exported bundles (RFC3161 style) and (B) deterministic rollback windows so customers can prove deletion happened. Can we cover both in MVP?

ben: Short answer: we can do export signing + object-lock for immutability easily. RFC3161 timestamping requires either an external TSA or building our own timestamp service (ops + legal implications). Which do we prefer?

arjun: Tech tradeoffs:
- Sign(manifest) + sha256 per file + S3 Object Lock (Governance) = cheap, fast, good for internal audits.
- RFC3161 adds a notarized timestamp from a third-party TSA, which auditors like for non-repudiation. It adds latency (RTT to TSA) and cost.

maya: Customers specifically mentioned ISO auditors wanting trusted timestamps. We should support TSA-stamped bundles as an opt-in for enterprise. Default: our signer + object-lock.

legal-bot: From legal: if we integrate TSA, pick one with widely accepted trust anchors. Add contract language around chain-of-custody: who requested the timestamp, operator identity, and an audit trail. Also include explicit consent for any escrowed unwrap flows.

zoe: Next topic: rollback/delete proof. Customer wants to show "we deleted X at time T and it can't be recovered". How do we prove that while also supporting legal-hold overrides?

ben: Implementation idea:
- Deletion is a workflow: admin toggles deletion -> system creates a signed deletion record (delete-manifest) with timestamp and affected object list -> object-lock prevents restoration until TTL expires.
- For legal holds we keep a separate signed hold record that overrides deletion. Proof of deletion is the signed record plus object-lock expiry stamps.

arjun: Edge case: cross-region replication. If a tenant is in multi-region, deletion must be coordinated and we need consistent proofs across copies. That requires synchronous replication for delete paths or a reconciliation proof (signed attestations from each region). More complexity/cost.

maya: Product constraint: MVP can support single-region guaranteed deletion proofs. Multi-region can be marked as "eventual" with attestation per-region in Phase 2. Call out in contracts.

legal-bot: Contract note: include language for what we provide as proof (signed manifests, object-lock metadata, timestamp certs) and the limitations (single-region strong proof vs multi-region best-effort). Customers must accept multi-region caveat in enterprise terms.

zoe: Operational question: who signs these manifests? A product service account? HSM-rooted key? We should avoid operator key signing to reduce audit risk.

ben: Prefer HSM-backed service signing keys stored in our KMS/HSM (not human-held). For TSA stamps we also keep cert chain for verification. We'll rotate signing keys with recorded key-rotation events included in provenance logs.

arjun: Also propose including a lightweight transparency log entry per export/delete (think: append-only ledger) that stores manifest-hash -> signer -> time. Could be internal (no public log). It helps detect accidental re-signing or replay.

maya: Nice. Keep it internal for now but design so we could publish hashes later. Acceptance criteria for provenance MVP:
- export pipeline produces signed bundle (manifest + per-file sha256) and stores signer cert chain
- S3 Object Lock configured per-tenant for archive exports (Governance mode)
- deletion workflow produces signed delete-manifest and stores proof in provenance index
- export UI shows timestamp (our signer) and allows TSA opt-in (enterprise) with note about latency/cost
- documentation: provenance spec + legal playbook + sample auditor verification steps

legal-bot: Add acceptance for BYOK interplay: if tenant uses BYOK for archive, we must define export-time unwrapping policy (escrow vs ephemeral unwrap). Contracts must require customer consent for any temporary unwrap for TSA stamping or deletion attestations.

ops-bot: Created ticket PROD-44200 "provenance-notarization-and-deletion-proof" assigned to @ben,@arjun due 6367990000. Link: https://rwd/issue/PROD-44200

zoe: Performance/scale calls: what's realistic for bundle signing at scale? Some pilots will request daily exports for many tenants. Need rate limits and cost model.

ben: Signing is CPU-light but TSA calls are external. We'll implement a queue with rate-limited TSA clients + ability to batch multiple manifests into a single TSA request (if acceptable). Default limits: 5 TSA-stamped exports/sec cluster-wide to avoid overloading provider. We'll surface backlog ETA in UI.

arjun: Metrics to track: export queue depth, TSA latency, manifest-signing success rate, provenance-index replication lag. We'll add alerts for >5% failure within a day.

maya: Billing model note: TSA-stamped export = base export charge + per-TSA-call surcharge. Deletion-attestation jobs billable as admin operations for enterprise. Finance will confirm numbers.

legal-bot: One more: include a key-loss attestation flow for BYOK archives: if keys lost, we will produce a notarized statement of non-decryptability (signed by Redwood) and include logs showing attempts and timestamps. Customers must accept that as part of BYOK T&C.

zoe: Good. Next steps:
- ben: prototype signer + manifest flow + object-lock config in staging and attach sample verification script to PROD-44200 (due in 5 working days)
- arjun: prototype provenance index + delete-manifest flow and test single-region proof (due same cadence)
- maya: draft product acceptance criteria + contract addenda with legal and finance and post to the ticket
- legal-bot: produce BYOK key-loss attestation language and TSA consent clause

ops-bot: Noted. All tasks aggregated under PROD-44200 and linked to pricing epic PRIC-7701.

zoe: Cool. We'll review the staging demo next Tue. If anyone has reference TSAs we should vet, drop links here. :mag_right:
